sections.title: Iran answers the blockade with terms and, reportedly, cyber
sections.body: Iran said on 23 November it will use all available means against the US blockade and could reopen Hormuz within two days if hostilities, the blockade and sanctions end. The Wall Street Journal reports US authorities are investigating suspected cyberattacks on up to 50 tankers, with Iran the prime suspect. The US Treasury sanctioned Iranian exchange houses the same day.

sections.title: Tankers burn north of Khasab
sections.body: The LPG tanker Tara Gas was hit on 16 and 17 November and abandoned, with an Indian seafarer missing; an ADNOC tanker was attacked on 17 November, one missing and 11 injured. CENTCOM said ships taking Iranian cargo at sea may be seized. The IEA called the Hormuz crisis the largest threat to energy security in history.

sections.title: The Crimean Bridge falls
sections.body: A Ukrainian missile and drone attack on 17 November dropped a road section of the Crimean Bridge into the Kerch Strait; a third attack on 19 November halted rail traffic. Russia struck Kyiv's two Dnipro bridges, and attacks killed 14 people across Ukraine on 17 November. A Pentagon official called deep strikes ineffective; Germany and Britain disagreed.

sections.title: Russian jets press on South Korea
sections.body: About five Russian warplanes entered South Korea's air defence zone on 24 November and approached Ulleung Island without breaching its airspace. Seoul issued its first preliminary air alert over Russian aircraft, scrambled fighters and summoned Russia's attaché. A week earlier Russian aircraft violated Japan's airspace and Tu-95 bombers landed in Vietnam.

sections.title: NATO answers Poland's incursions
sections.body: A Russian drone entered Polish airspace late on 23 November, which Poland's deputy defence minister called deliberate, three days after Russian cruise missiles fell in the south-east; Kyiv Post reports all three were Kh-101s. NATO's council agreed to give Poland an early-warning aircraft and will weigh further air-defence requests next week.

sections.title: Gaza's ceasefire line is crossed
sections.body: Israeli tanks crossed the ceasefire line into Hamas-held central Gaza on 18 November, the first such armoured incursion of the truce, displacing 5,200 people; Hamas called it a blatant violation. Israel killed Hamas's Rafah brigade commander on 14 November. In Yemen, the Saudi-led coalition struck 60 Houthi targets.

key_developments: Russian warplanes neared South Korea's Ulleung Island; Seoul issued its first air alert over Russian aircraft.
NATO agreed to give Poland an AWACS after a Russian drone entered its airspace again on 23 November.
The US blacklisted Megaspeed and six Southeast Asian firms over suspected Nvidia chip diversion.
US officials are probing suspected Iranian cyberattacks on up to 50 ships, the WSJ reports.
Iran set terms to reopen Hormuz within two days and vowed all means against the blockade.
Moscow warned Estonia of 'the brink of an open war' over its border closure.
since_last_visit_brief: Russian warplanes neared South Korea's Ulleung Island, drawing Seoul's first air alert, and NATO agreed to send Poland an early-warning aircraft.
